statement: For design/analysis, treat any op amp in a negative-feedback configuration as ideal: zero current into both input terminals (i1 = i2 = 0) and zero differential input voltage (v1 = v2). Negative feedback exists only when the output is fed back to the inverting terminal; the op amp must also be powered (V+ and V- supply pins connected) since output current returns through the supplies.
condition: Op amp operating in the linear region with a feedback path from output to the inverting input
erc_rule: Every op amp in a linear amplifier role must have (a) a feedback network connecting its output to its inverting input, and (b) both power-supply pins connected; the virtual-short (v+ = v-) and zero-input-current assumptions are only valid then

source.book: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, 7th International Student Edition (Alexander & Sadiku)
source.section: 5.3 Ideal Op Amp (Eqs. 5.5-5.7); 5.2 for feedback definition

statement: An op amp's output voltage magnitude cannot exceed its supply voltage; linear operation requires -VCC <= vo <= VCC, otherwise the output saturates at +VCC or -VCC. Check the computed output against the rails when choosing gain and supply.
condition: Any op-amp circuit; check computed vo = A*vd (closed-loop: gain x input) against supply rails
formula: -VCC <= vo <= VCC (linear region); vo = +VCC (positive saturation); vo = -VCC (negative saturation)
erc_rule: Flag if |expected output voltage| = |closed-loop gain x max input| exceeds the connected supply voltage VCC — the stage will clip

source.book: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, 7th International Student Edition (Alexander & Sadiku)

statement: Inverting amplifier: input through R1 to the inverting input, feedback resistor Rf from inverting input to output, noninverting input grounded. Closed-loop gain is -Rf/R1, set entirely by the two external resistors.
condition: Ideal op amp; vi drives inverting input via R1; Rf from inverting input to output; noninverting input at ground

values.worked_example_5_3: R1 = 10 kOhm, Rf = 25 kOhm -> gain = -2.5; vi = 0.5 V -> vo = -1.25 V, input-resistor current 50 uA

source.book: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, 7th International Student Edition (Alexander & Sadiku)

statement: Noninverting amplifier: input at the noninverting terminal, R1 from inverting input to ground, Rf from inverting input to output; gain is 1 + Rf/R1 (always positive, >= 1). With Rf = 0 (short) and/or R1 = infinity (open) the circuit becomes a unity-gain voltage follower (vo = vi), used as a high-input-impedance buffer to isolate cascaded stages and eliminate interstage loading.
condition: Ideal op amp; vi applied directly to noninverting input; R1 from inverting input to ground; Rf from inverting input to output
formula: vo = (1 + Rf/R1) * vi;  follower special case: vo = vi when Rf = 0 or R1 = infinite

source.book: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, 7th International Student Edition (Alexander & Sadiku)

statement: Inverting summing amplifier: multiple inputs v1..vn each through their own resistor R1..Rn into the inverting node, one feedback resistor Rf; the output is the inverted weighted sum with each weight Rf/Rk, so per-input gain is set independently by that input's resistor.
condition: Ideal op amp; all input resistors join at the inverting-input summing node (virtual ground); noninverting input grounded; Rf from summing node to output

source.book: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, 7th International Student Edition (Alexander & Sadiku)

statement: Difference amplifier (v1 via R1 to inverting node with feedback R2; v2 via R3 to noninverting node with R4 to ground): general output is vo = R2(1+R1/R2)/(R1(1+R3/R4)) * v2 - (R2/R1) * v1. Common-mode rejection (vo = 0 when v1 = v2) requires the resistor-ratio balance R1/R2 = R3/R4, which reduces the output to vo = (R2/R1)(v2 - v1); with R2 = R1 and R3 = R4 it is a unity-gain subtractor vo = v2 - v1.
condition: Ideal op amp; for common-mode rejection the ratios must satisfy R1/R2 = R3/R4
formula: vo = (R2/R1)(v2 - v1) when R1/R2 = R3/R4; subtractor: vo = v2 - v1 when R2 = R1 and R3 = R4

values.worked_practice_5_7: gain 7.5 realized with R1 = R3 = 20 kOhm, R2 = R4 = 150 kOhm

erc_rule: In a difference-amplifier topology, flag if R1/R2 != R3/R4 — common-mode signals will not be rejected

source.book: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, 7th International Student Edition (Alexander & Sadiku)

statement: First-order passive RC filter: taking the output across the capacitor of a series RC gives a low-pass (H = 1/(1+jwRC)); taking it across the resistor gives a high-pass (H = jwRC/(1+jwRC)). Both have cutoff (half-power) frequency wc = 1/(RC) rad/s — equivalently fc = wc/(2pi) = 1/(2*pi*R*C) Hz using w0 = 2*pi*f0 — where |H| falls to 1/sqrt(2) (70.71%) of maximum. Maximum gain of any passive filter is 1.
condition: Series R and C driven by the source; output node choice (capacitor vs. resistor) selects low-pass vs. high-pass
formula: wc = 1/(RC) [rad/s]; fc = 1/(2*pi*R*C) [Hz]; |H(wc)| = 1/sqrt(2); low-pass H(w) = 1/(1 + jwRC), high-pass H(w) = jwRC/(1 + jwRC)

source.book: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits, 7th International Student Edition (Alexander & Sadiku)

statement: Active first-order filters built on the inverting op-amp stage: low-pass uses Zi = Ri and Zf = Rf parallel Cf, giving dc gain -Rf/Ri and corner wc = 1/(Rf*Cf) (independent of Ri, so multiple inputs with different Ri can be summed without moving the corner); high-pass uses Zi = Ri in series with Ci and Zf = Rf, giving high-frequency gain -Rf/Ri and corner wc = 1/(Ri*Ci). Active filters can exceed unity gain but are practically limited to about 100 kHz.
condition: Inverting op-amp configuration H = -Zf/Zi with one reactive element; ideal op amp
formula: Low-pass: H(w) = -(Rf/Ri) * 1/(1 + jwCf*Rf), wc = 1/(Rf*Cf); High-pass: H(w) = -jwCi*Rf/(1 + jwCi*Ri), wc = 1/(Ri*Ci)

statement: Practical op-amp parameter ranges (Table 5.1): open-loop gain A typically 10^5 to 10^8 (ideal: infinite), input resistance Ri typically 10^5 to 10^13 Ohm (ideal: infinite), output resistance Ro typically 10 to 100 Ohm (ideal: 0), supply voltage VCC typically 5 to 24 V. Concrete 741 values used in the book's worked example: A = 200,000, Ri = 2 MOhm, Ro = 50 Ohm.
condition: Selecting or modeling a real (nonideal) op amp; use for sanity-checking part parameters
